cards.front: Recall a key point about Media & Technology
cards.back: Technology has always shaped media — from the printing press to broadcast radio to the internet. Each technological shift transforms how media is produced, distributed, and consumed.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Media & Technology
cards.back: Digital transformation: the shift from analogue to digital has affected every media form — digital cameras, non-linear editing, streaming, online publishing, and social media.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Media & Technology
cards.back: Convergence: smartphones combine multiple media forms (camera, music player, social media, web browser, TV). This has changed audience behaviour — we carry entire media libraries in our pockets.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Media & Technology
cards.back: Streaming revolution: Netflix, Amazon Prime, Disney+ have disrupted cinema, broadcast TV, and physical media. Content is available on demand, anywhere, on any device.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Media & Technology
cards.back: Social media as a media platform: Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube are now major media distributors, reaching billions of users. They blur the line between producer and audience.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Media & Technology
cards.back: Algorithmic distribution: social media and streaming platforms use algorithms to personalise content feeds, creating filter bubbles and influencing what audiences see.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Media & Technology
cards.back: AI and media: artificial intelligence is used for content recommendation, automated news writing, deepfake technology, and targeted advertising. This raises ethical questions about authenticity and manipulation.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Media & Technology
cards.back: Big data: media companies collect vast amounts of user data to personalise content, target advertising, and make commissioning decisions. This raises privacy concerns.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Media & Technology
cards.back: The attention economy: digital platforms compete for user attention, designing features (autoplay, notifications, infinite scroll) that maximise engagement. This has been linked to addiction concerns.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Media & Technology
cards.back: User-generated content: technology enables audiences to create and distribute content — YouTube, TikTok, podcasts, blogs. This democratises media but also creates quality and misinformation challenges.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Media & Technology
cards.back: Virtual and augmented reality: emerging technologies offer new media experiences. VR cinema and AR gaming create immersive forms that challenge traditional media conventions.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Media & Technology
cards.back: Technology and access: while digital technology has increased access, the digital divide means not everyone benefits equally — age, income, location, and disability affect participation.

cards.front: What should you know about media studies exam tips — media & technology?
cards.back: 1. For Media & Technology, use media terminology precisely (e.g. connotation, denotation, representation, ideology) 2. Always analyse how media language creates meaning for specific audiences 3. Reference specific examples from set products to support your analysis 4. When evaluating Media & Technology, consider the role of media industries and cultural contexts 5. For extended answers, debate different interpretations before reaching your own
